input.area: Admin notes panel — proximity-hover (macOS-dock) target for the row of collapsed note pills inside NotesPanel.
components: NotesPanel (default export, client component) — renders `<aside className={styles.panel}>` containing `<header>`, `<div className={styles.list}>` (the pill rail), and the `+ Add note` button. Owns `notes`, `expandedId`, `mobileOpen`, `busy`, `error`. Mounted from the admin editor (see EditorWithNotes.tsx).

NoteCard (default export, client component) — receives `note`, `expanded`, `onExpand`, `onCollapse`, `onChange`, `onDelete`. Renders one of two outer divs: collapsed `<div className={`${styles.card} ${styles.collapsed}`} data-color={note.color}>` (pill) or expanded variant. Collapsed children: `<button className={styles.pillBody}>` with `<span className={styles.dot}/>` + `<span className={styles.pillTitle}>` and a sibling 3-dot `menu` (`.menuWrap`).
NOTE_COLORS const + DotsGlyph/CheckGlyph/NotesGlyph/CrossGlyph inline SVG helpers (NoteCard.tsx, NotesPanel.tsx).

.list (NotesPanel.module.css L65–78): `display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:8px; flex:1 1 auto; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto; padding:4px 0;` — vertical stack of pills with a vertical scrollbar. Note: this is a COLUMN flex, so dock-style proximity will be along the Y axis (cursor's vertical distance to each pill's vertical center), not horizontal like a real macOS dock. Worth confirming with the user if they wanted horizontal. Each collapsed pill (NoteCard.module.css L7–22, L32–49): `.card` sets `transition: border-color, transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 220ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)`. `.collapsed` is a row-flex pill (`flex-direction:row; align-items:center; gap:4px; padding:4px 6px 4px 12px; border-radius:var(--radius-pill)`). On `:hover` it sets `border-color: var(--note-color); transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 6px 14px -8px color-mix(... var(--note-color) 55%, transparent)`. On `:active` it resets transform and clears the shadow. There is no `width`/`height`/`scale` declaration on the pill — its size is intrinsic to content (the title text). The expanded card uses `animation: noteExpandIn 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) both;` on mount/swap. @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) in BOTH modules zeroes transitions/animations, including the pill hover transform + shadow.
input.integrationPoints:
Attach cursor listeners on the `.list` container in NotesPanel.tsx (the `<div className={styles.list}>` at line 146). That element already owns the pill stack and the scroll, so its bounding rect + scrollTop is the right local coordinate space. Concrete wiring suggestion:

  - Add a `listRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)` in NotesPanel and `<div ref={listRef} className={styles.list} ...>`.
  - Listen `onPointerMove` / `onPointerLeave` on that div (NOT `mousemove` on window — avoids work when cursor is elsewhere on screen).
  - Inside the move handler, query `listRef.current.querySelectorAll(':scope > div[data-color]')` (or expose a `data-note-pill` attribute on the collapsed `.card` to avoid grabbing the expanded card when one is open) to get every pill, read each `getBoundingClientRect()`, compute the distance from cursor Y to the pill's center Y, and drive a falloff (e.g. gaussian over ~120–180px) per-pill.
  - For GSAP: use a `gsap.quickTo()` per pill on `scale` (and optionally `y`) for a per-frame interpolation that matches dock feel; reset on `pointerleave`.
  - NoteCard collapsed branch should accept either a ref-forwarding outer div or a stable selector (`data-note-pill` attribute) so the parent can enumerate without a child-side re-render. Easiest non-invasive change: spread a `data-note-pill="true"` on the collapsed `<div className={... styles.collapsed}>` (NoteCard.tsx L176–179).
  - Skip the effect entirely when `expandedId` is set (only one pill in the rail then — nothing to magnify) OR when `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`.
  - The `.list` is `overflow-y:auto` and lives inside a sticky aside whose `top` animates (`hasExpanded`), so use `getBoundingClientRect()` each move rather than caching positions — pill rects shift during scroll and during the 260ms panel growth transition.

Other mount/data context: the panel is rendered by `EditorWithNotes.tsx` and shows up on the admin story/chapter editor. The list of pills is bound to React state (`notes`) and mutates (add/delete/optimistic update), so any cached pill node array on the GSAP side must re-sync on each render — recommend re-querying inside the pointermove handler (cheap, small N) or running a layout effect keyed on `notes.length` to refresh the quickTo map.
input.notes:
EXISTING TRANSITIONS THAT WILL COLLIDE WITH GSAP — call out before wiring:

1. `.card` (NoteCard.module.css L18–22) already has `transition: transform 180ms ... , box-shadow 220ms ...`. If GSAP writes `transform` every frame on pointermove, the CSS transition will fight it — each GSAP tween will be re-eased by the CSS transition, producing a perceptible lag/smear. Two options: (a) clear the CSS transition for `transform` on the pills while the proximity effect is active (toggle a class on `.list` that sets `transition: border-color var(--transition-fast)` only on its `.collapsed` children), or (b) drive a CSS custom property (e.g. `--dock-scale`) from GSAP and let CSS apply `transform: scale(var(--dock-scale, 1))` — but the existing `:hover` rule writes `transform: translateY(-1px)` which would clobber `scale()` unless rewritten to be additive.

2. `.collapsed:hover` (L39–45) sets `transform: translateY(-1px)` and a colored `box-shadow`. With proximity hover, EVERY pill near the cursor needs the lift, not just the one being `:hover`'d. Either (a) supersede the `:hover` rule (drop the transform + shadow from `:hover`, let GSAP own them entirely and key both off proximity distance), or (b) coordinate — keep `:hover` for the focal pill and have GSAP only animate the neighbours. Cleanest is (a): the dock metaphor IS proximity, so `:hover` becomes redundant.

3. `.collapsed:active` resets transform to `translateY(0) scale(0.995)`. If GSAP owns the transform during the press, the click squish needs to be expressed as a quickTo too, or `:active` should bump CSS specificity via `!important` (last resort).

4. `.expanded` runs a 200ms `noteExpandIn` keyframe animation on swap (L106). When the user clicks a magnified pill, GSAP should release that pill's tween (reset to scale 1) BEFORE the React state swap so the keyframe animation starts from the natural transform, otherwise the expand-in will visually pop.

5. The panel itself transitions `max-height/min-height/top` over 260ms when `hasExpanded` toggles (NotesPanel.module.css L28–32, L38–45). During that 260ms, pill `getBoundingClientRect()` positions change every frame — proximity math must read live rects, not memoized ones.

6. `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` blocks (NoteCard.module.css L333–348, NotesPanel.module.css L242–252) explicitly zero the hover transform/shadow. The GSAP effect must mirror this: bail out of the listener install if reduced-motion is requested, and respond to `matchMedia` change events (writer can toggle this OS-level mid-session).

7. The pill stack is `flex-direction: column` (vertical), so this is a *vertical* proximity dock. Real macOS dock is horizontal. If the user wants horizontal magnification, the `.list` flex direction needs flipping (which conflicts with `overflow-y` scroll behavior) — worth surfacing as a clarification before building.

Recommendation: have GSAP own `scale` (+ optional `y`) and `box-shadow` via JS-set inline styles, REMOVE the existing `.collapsed:hover` `transform`/`box-shadow` rules so there's a single source of truth, keep CSS for `border-color` on hover (cheap, doesn't fight transform), and gate the whole thing behind a reduced-motion check + `expandedId == null` check.
